assignments.name: classifierPrompt
assignments.value:
You triage incoming support e-mails into EGroupware Tracker tickets.

Answer with a single JSON object, no prose, no markdown fence:
{
  "queue": one of "Bugs", "Feature Requests", "Patches",
  "category": one of "Tracker", "API", or null,
  "priority": integer 1-9 (1 lowest, 5 normal, 9 highest; base it on real business impact, not on the sender shouting),
  "title": imperative one-line summary, max 70 chars, no "Re:" and no ticket ids,
  "summary": at most two sentences describing the problem,
  "language": ISO 639-1 code of the mail
}

Rules:
- "Bugs" = something is broken or behaves wrongly. "Feature Requests" = asks for something new.
  "Patches" = the sender supplies a fix, diff or pull request.
- Several people blocked, data loss or a production outage -> priority 8-9.
  One person inconvenienced, or a question -> priority 3-4. Anything else -> 5.

nodes.name: Config
nodes.notes: mailAccount = acc_id from GET /mail. mailFolder accepts either the opaque folder id or, since upstream dbcff1056d/84ad5102ad, the literal name - "INBOX", or "INBOX::Sent" for a subfolder.

nodes.name: List new mail
nodes.notes: GET the folder listing; new-vs-seen is decided in "Split new mail" - filter[after] is a no-op on the JmapShim.

nodes.name: Fetch body
nodes.notes: The list endpoint returns headers only; bodyValues come from the single-email GET.

nodes.name: POST reply
nodes.notes: An answer to a ticket mail becomes a Tracker reply, not an edit of the description.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify(Object.assign({ title: $json.title, description: $json.description, priority: $json.priority, status: "Open", privacy: "public" }, $json.trackerId ? { tracker: $json.trackerId } : {}, $json.llmCategory ? { category: $json.llmCategory } : {})) }}

nodes.name: POST create ticket
nodes.notes: status must be the capitalised label 'Open' — the lowercase values in the main repo's doc/REST-CalDAV-CardDAV/Tracker.md are rejected with 422.

nodes.name: Upload attachment
nodes.notes: POST, not PUT — a PUT here is parsed as a JSON link payload and fails with 422 'Error parsing JSON'.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ model: $json.llmModel, temperature: 0, max_tokens: 400, messages: [ { role: "system", content: $json.classifierPrompt }, { role: "user", content: "Subject: " + $json.subject + "\n\n" + $json.bodyText } ] }) }}

nodes.name: Classify (LLM)
nodes.notes: EGroupware AI proxy. neverError is on so a proxy outage degrades to the keyword rules instead of losing the mail.

nodes.name: Download attachment
nodes.notes: A JMAP Email lists attachments as blob references, so the bytes need this second GET.

nodes.name: Known tickets
nodes.notes: The de-dup record: every ticket carries the mail key it came from in its description.

nodes.name: GET ticket
nodes.notes: neverError: a 404 here is an expected outcome (the ticket was deleted), not a failure.

parameters.content:
## 1 · Read new mail
Every minute n8n lists the **INBOX** through EGroupware's mail REST API, skips anything already filed as a ticket, and fetches each new mail's body.

## 2 · Answer to an existing ticket
Subject carries **[#id]** → the mail is added as a **reply** on that ticket — never a second ticket.

## 3 · New ticket — AI triage
An LLM decides the **queue**, the **priority** and an English **title**; the ticket is created over the Tracker REST API.

## 4 · Attachments
Files are pulled from the mail and linked to the ticket.
